series.title: Signal metrology: the grader as a measurement device
Grader structure: is this thing a scalar, and what is it made of?
Grader white-box: the existing battery, re-typed
The estimator: where a good reward becomes a bad gradient
Adversarial pressure, and the monitor as a target
The frontier: what would happen if we optimised

instruments.name: Curl mass and the harmonic split
instruments.headline: How much preference structure no scalar can carry, and how much of that is fixable.
instruments.invarianceGroup: `reward.affine`, `group.permutation` (not invariant under a change of the comparison design, which must be reported: CALIPER line 1459)

envelope.unconditionalJustification: ASSAY line 1650 prints "at least 11 replications per pair for the nulls", which is a sample-size requirement and therefore a refusal with a stated n rather than a regime condition. E23 settles that distinction for N3 and it holds here.

ladder.estimator: curl mass from a single pass

baselines: the transitive baseline, MANDATORY and reported on every reading. A comparison recorded as a bare win is a sign and not a margin, so a transitive ±1 tournament on `K_n` already carries curl mass exactly `(n-2)/(3n)`, which is 5/21 at seven items. A curl mass without this floor beside it is uninterpretable, and the campaign's 0.214 sits on the floor to fifteen significant figures with zero cyclic triples in the corpus. SPEC-ERRATA E32.
a Bradley-Terry fit's residual

the random-profile null, by simulation through the identical pipeline. The `(5/6)|E|` constant printed in §3.6 is unsourced and could not be derived or reproduced, so it is not used and not quoted. SPEC-ERRATA E33.
a transitive-plus-measured-flip-rate simulation
instruments.killCondition: if Null C shows the curl component does not replicate across split halves, in which case 0.214 is measurement error and the instrument reports a noise level instead.
instruments.says: "21.4% of this grader's preference structure is not expressible by any scalar. Of that, 6 points are curl (the judge is locally cyclic) and 15 are harmonic (your comparison design has holes and could be fixed by comparing different pairs)."

instruments.name: Policy readout recoverability
instruments.headline: What a linear readout of the policy's own residual stream recovers, against the black-box bank on the same items.

envelope.unconditionalJustification: a cross-fitted probe on a fixed item set depends on no property of the optimisation that produced the items. What it does depend on is label quality and class balance, and both are checked in preflight and refused by name rather than declared as regime conditions, because neither is a property of a run.

ladder.estimator: a ridge readout of the residual stream at a named site, cross-fitted over folds, scored against the black-box baseline bank on the same items with the error correlation between the two methods' per-item margins
ladder.bias: the penalty is fixed rather than tuned, at alpha times the mean eigenvalue of the training Gram, because a hyperparameter chosen on the evaluation set is a fitted parameter the baseline bank exists to count. That makes the reading a floor on what a tuned probe would recover.
ladder.cost: one forward pass per item plus a ridge solve; no grader calls

baselines: the six-member black-box bank, on the same items
the best single baseline, which is what the incremental record is scored against
instruments.killCondition: if the probe never beats the black-box bank and is never decorrelated from it on any real subject, a linear readout of the residual stream is not carrying anything the text does not, and the instrument reports that rather than the field assuming otherwise.
instruments.says: "The probe reads 0.536 where the best black-box baseline reads 0.964, at an error correlation of +0.21 and an ensemble gain of exactly zero. On this run, opening the network bought nothing."

instruments.name: The forecast calibration ledger
instruments.headline: The score of the library's own forecasts, in public, with the honest starting position printed at the top.

envelope.unconditionalJustification: a proper scoring rule is a function of forecasts and realised outcomes and of nothing about the run that produced them, so no regime condition bears on it. The conditions that matter here are on the forecasts, and the barrier enforces them at construction rather than at scoring.

ladder.estimator: the half-Brier score with the Murphy decomposition into reliability, resolution and uncertainty, a skill score against each mandatory baseline with a bootstrap interval, a reliability diagram, and the expected loss saved under the forecast's own DecisionSpec
ladder.bias: unbiased for the forecasts it is given, and it says how many resolutions went void rather than scoring them as misses, because dropping a call and scoring it wrong are different numbers and the reader has to see which was done

instruments.name: Instrument effect
instruments.headline: The overhead this measurement imposed, per step, as a term in the uncertainty budget. **No competitor has published an overhead number of any kind**, so a monitor with a measured one would be the first.

instruments.name: Dumb-baseline bank
instruments.headline: String match, length, TF-IDF, n-gram diversity, a scaffolded black-box prompt, the gradient-norm peak. Every claim ships against all six. The reason is a single published case: a probe reported at AUC 0.998 on a task where a zero-parameter string match scores 100%, whose author's summary is "the probe detects the hack, and the detection is empty."

instruments.name: Semantic placebo
instruments.headline: A coherent but irrelevant direction, not a random Gaussian one. Mandatory on every steering and ablation claim, because a vampires-versus-werewolves direction suppressed deployment-time hacking to 0.000 exactly as well as the real direction.

instruments.name: Matched positive control
instruments.headline: A null without an identically-powered positive control is indistinguishable from an underpowered experiment. `NO_MATCHED_CONTROL` is a refusal reason. The library's own susceptibility card at accepted power 0.13 conspicuously lacked one.

instruments.name: Reasoning-stripped ablation
instruments.headline: For anything that reads text, because a leading detector drops from AUC 0.9467 to 0.6213 once natural-language reasoning is removed from its input, and reviewers will run this if we do not.

instruments.name: Uncertainty budget
instruments.headline: The GUM table, lint-enforced to compose, with the largest term named. It is almost never sampling noise.

instruments.name: Interlaboratory comparison
instruments.headline: HuggingFace against vLLM, eager against compiled, two seeds, two precisions. Report `s_L` and the Birge ratio beside every reading.

instruments.name: Incremental validity
instruments.headline: §6.4. Required on every white-box reading.

instruments.name: Power and minimum detectable effect
instruments.headline: Before the run, not after. Three of five standard power calculators are roughly 2x wrong for close paired model comparisons, and the resolution ratio `q = N/N*` says outright when a leaderboard row is not resolved. Also carry the detection-band lesson: position bias is statistically detectable only within roughly a 60% to 95% base-accuracy window, so **absence of signal above that band should be read as "not measurable", not as "unbiased"**, and that logic applies to several of the library's own refuted cards.

instruments.name: Rung disagreement, published
instruments.headline: When two rungs of the same ladder disagree on the same data, that difference is the cheap method's transfer uncertainty. It becomes a `Transfer` row and it composes into the calibration chain. Nobody publishes this.

instruments.name: The reward-versus-gold frontier
instruments.headline: The whole frontier is estimable before any optimisation is run, from n base-policy rollouts scored by both channels.
instruments.accessMin: GRADER:QUERY + GOLD:QUERY + POLICY:QUERY, on the same n samples

ladder.estimator: self-normalised importance sampling over the tilt family; every reported number is a ratio of weighted means with the max-subtraction applied before exponentiating
ladder.bias: consistent, downward-biased in variance at small ESS; the self-normalised ratio is biased at order 1/ESS and the bias grows exactly where the horizon is about to refuse
ladder.cost: n grader calls and n gold calls, both reusable across every lambda on the sweep

baselines: HedgeTune (arXiv 2506.19248), run on the same samples. This is mandatory rather than a citation, because it is a bisection and Newton solver for the same turning point consuming the same data, and the two turning-point estimates are reported side by side.
the untilted base-policy gold mean at lambda = 0
a linear extrapolation from the first two points of the sweep, which is the null under which the curve has no shape (CALIPER E1, line 1636)
instruments.killCondition: if HedgeTune and the cumulant estimate agree within their intervals on every grader tested, report HedgeTune and drop the second estimator. CALIPER E1 (line 1638) states the stronger kill, for the layer rather than for the estimator: if the predicted turn does not match the realised turn on any open model where both are measurable, at any horizon, Level 0 is descriptive rather than predictive.
instruments.says: "Gold peaks at KL = 1.8 nats and we can see out to 3.1 before ESS falls below floor."

instruments.name: The visibility horizon
instruments.headline: Where a tilt extrapolation goes blind, which nobody states.

ladder.estimator: Kish ESS(lambda) = (sum w_i)^2 / sum w_i^2, swept until it crosses a stated floor, default 0.05 of n
ladder.bias: approximately unbiased as a summary of the realised weights, being a property of the sample rather than an estimate of a population quantity. The envelope still requires LIGHT_TAILED because the horizon is reported in nats, and the KL it bounds exists only where K(lambda) does. On a heavy-tailed reward the empirical K is a finite sum converging to nothing.
ladder.cost: none beyond N1's n grader calls

baselines: the raw sample size n, which is what a frontier reported without a horizon implicitly claims
the naive count of rollouts with nonzero weight
instruments.killCondition: if the horizon never binds before the sweep's own range on any real grader, it is a formality rather than an instrument and it collapses into N1's reporting range.
instruments.says: "Past lambda = 2.4 this instrument declines to answer. n/ESS = 20."

instruments.name: Reward tail index
instruments.headline: The precondition the whole tilt layer rests on, measured rather than assumed.

envelope.unconditionalJustification: The Hill estimator on the upper tail depends on no regime condition. What it depends on is exceedance count, and an inadequate one is a refusal with a stated required n rather than a violated envelope, because the quantity stays well defined and only the estimate is unavailable.

ladder.estimator: Hill estimator over a threshold sweep, reported as a Hill plot with the stability protocol rather than as a point estimate at one k
ladder.bias: upward-biased at small k and threshold-sensitive; the plot is the reading and a single k is not
ladder.cost: n grader calls, shared with N1

baselines: a light-tailed parametric fit (exponential upper tail) at the same threshold, for contrast
instruments.killCondition: if every grader tested is unambiguously light-tailed, the instrument becomes a precondition check rather than a reported quantity, and it renders as an envelope line on the card instead of a row.
instruments.says: "Hill gamma-hat = 0.19 [0.12, 0.27]. Light-tailed assumption holds."

instruments.name: Surrogate conditions and the concomitant of best-of-n
instruments.headline: Falsifiable conditions on the proxy beat a predicted turning point, and best-of-n Goodhart is a concomitant problem nobody has recognised as one.
instruments.accessMin: GRADER:QUERY + GOLD:QUERY, on the same n samples

ladder.estimator: the four surrogate-endpoint criteria as explicit testable conditions on the joint distribution of (r, g, treatment), each returning pass, fail or untestable; and the exact finite-n concomitant expectation of the maximum-of-selected-concomitants problem
ladder.bias: the concomitant expectation is exact at the stated n given the joint sample; the criteria are verdicts rather than estimates and carry no bias direction
ladder.cost: none beyond N1's n grader and gold calls

baselines: the marginal proxy-gold correlation, which is what practice currently looks at and which cannot distinguish a mediating surrogate from a merely correlated one
simulation of best-of-n at the same n, to check the exact expression
instruments.killCondition: if every criterion returns untestable on every real grader for want of an intervention, the checklist is a research note rather than an instrument and only the concomitant reading ships.
instruments.says: "Fails criterion 4: the proxy does not fully mediate the treatment effect on gold. At n = 64, expected gold at the proxy-argmax is 0.71 [0.66, 0.75], exactly."

instruments.name: Optimal component weights
instruments.headline: Nobody sets a reward component's weight from that component's measured noise, and the formula that does has been sitting in contract theory since 1991.
instruments.accessMin: GRADER: REPLICATE, for Sigma. Every other parameter is stated or swept

ladder.estimator: alpha* = [M C''^-1 M' + r Sigma]^-1 M C''^-1 B', with Sigma from A2 and the other four parameters stated or swept. The diagonal form alpha_i = B_i / (1 + r C_ii sigma_i^2) and the unmeasurable-task form are special cases of the same solve and are checked against it.
ladder.bias: exact given the parameters, and the parameters are where the error lives. The recommendation is a deterministic function of five inputs of which one is measured, so its uncertainty is dominated by the four that are not, and the sweep rather than an interval is what reports it.

baselines: equal weights across components, which is what a composite with no analysis uses
weights proportional to B', which is what weighting by importance means and is this recommendation with the noise term deleted
instruments.killCondition: if the recommended weights are within measurement error of the value-proportional baseline on every real composite tested, the noise term is doing no work and the instrument is a restatement of B'.
instruments.says: "skywork-v2-qwen3-8b keeps 0.141 of the weight its value alone would buy it, and armorm keeps 0.926, decided by measured noise on components of equal stated value. Where one task cannot be measured, the correction sends the measurable component's weight to exactly zero, and only when the two tasks are equally valuable."

instruments.name: The equal-compensation table
instruments.headline: Which component of a composite reward the policy is being paid least to work on.
instruments.accessMin: GRADER: RECORD for the weights; POLICY: CONTROL for a measured sensitivity

ladder.estimator: kappa_i = alpha_i mu'_i from a stated sensitivity, normalised by the largest kappa across components; the starved component is argmin kappa. A stated mu' makes the table a conditional statement and every row says which of the two it is on.
ladder.bias: exact given mu'. A stated mu' is an assumption and the reading names it as one.
ladder.cost: free. Arithmetic on parameters the caller already holds.

ladder.estimator: the same table with mu' from a measured weight sweep
ladder.bias: a finite-difference sensitivity, so it inherits the sweep's step size

baselines: the weights read as commissions, which is what treating a weight as an incentive assumes and is this table under mu' = 1
equal weights, which is what the table would say if the composite had not been tuned
instruments.killCondition: if the commission ratio is within a few percent of 1 for every component of every real composite tested, composites are already equal-compensating and the table is a formality. It does not fire here; the spread is 0.033.
instruments.says: "The commissions are 0.037, 0.421 and 1.117. armorm is starved: it pays the policy under four percent of what the best-paying component pays for the same unit of capacity, and its stated weight of one third is not the incentive it delivers."

instruments.name: The sorting cutoff
instruments.headline: Do not put a noisy judge and a crisp unit test in the same weighted sum, with the threshold at which that stops being a slogan.
instruments.accessMin: GRADER: REPLICATE for Sigma; POLICY: CONTROL for the sensitivities

ladder.estimator: exhaustive maximisation of the summed contract value B_g^2 / [2 C (1 + r C N_g)] over partitions, with the interval partition in rho order computed alongside and the two compared, so the sorting theorem's own claim is checked rather than assumed. Comparisons across the number of contracts carry the capacity correction C -> k C, without which splitting compares one agent against several and looks free.
ladder.bias: exact given the parameters. Above the enumeration limit only the interval scan runs and the reading records that the check did not happen.
ladder.cost: free. Arithmetic on parameters the caller already holds.

baselines: one contract holding every component, which is what every composite reward is
one contract per component, which is the other extreme and is usually worse
instruments.killCondition: if the single-contract baseline is optimal on every real composite tested, splitting never pays and the instrument reports a cutoff nobody should act on.
instruments.says: "Split at rho = 0.183: armorm in one stage, tulu-rm and skywork-v2-qwen3-8b in another. Keeping skywork-v2-qwen3-8b in one sum with the rest multiplies every other component's incentive intensity by 0.49, and splitting is worth +141% against the single weighted sum at the same total capacity."

instruments.name: Noise and angle, per component
instruments.headline: Every reward component needs at least two numbers, a noise and an angle, and no RLHF tooling separates them.
instruments.accessMin: GRADER: REPLICATE for Sigma; POLICY: CONTROL for the sensitivity matrix

ladder.estimator: n_i = sigma_i^2 / mu'_i^2 from A2's variance components and the sensitivity matrix; congruity is the cosine between the i-th row of M and B', with the whole-contract cosine between M' alpha and B' reported beside it. A single component's cosine cannot reach 1 when the value direction spreads over several tasks, so distortion is measured against the clean-measure reference B_i / ||B'|| rather than against 1.
ladder.bias: exact given the parameters. Congruity is degenerate under a diagonal M, where it equals the normalised benefit vector, and the reading refuses to call that a measurement of distortion.
ladder.cost: free. Arithmetic on parameters the caller already holds.

baselines: the marginal correlation between each component and the outcome, which is what practice looks at and which cannot separate a noisy measure from a distorted one
the component's raw variance, which is the noise half with the sensitivity left in and is therefore not comparable across components
instruments.killCondition: Fires on this subject, and the reading says which half is a measurement. The tasks are identified one-to-one with the components, so M is diagonal by construction and every distortion is exactly zero; the off-diagonal path is exercised on a constructed M that is labelled synthetic. Recorded rather than hidden, and it is also why the noise half must be divided by the squared sensitivity: SPEC-ERRATA E47 found the diagonal weight formula is not scale free, and on this panel the three components' raw noise variances differ by a factor of 74,890, which is almost entirely the scale each model emits on, while their effort-equivalent noise differs by 80, which is the real difference.
instruments.says: "The three components' effort-equivalent noise is 0.029, 1.172 and 2.296, so tulu-rm and skywork-v2-qwen3-8b want lower weights. Their distortions are exactly zero, and by construction rather than by measurement: the sensitivity matrix is diagonal here, so the angle half is not a reading this subject can support."
